profiles.name: Bronze
profiles.label: Baseline
profiles.for: any static surface (docs, small tools); an afternoon's work, no CI/signing
profiles.adds: egress boundary, CSP lockdown + anti-framing property, core security headers, no secrets in output, no known-CVE deps, no pre-consent telemetry, self-hosted fonts, in-browser-only output

profiles.name: Silver
profiles.label: Hardened
profiles.for: tools handling user data or commercially deployed
profiles.adds: supply-chain integrity, CI hardening, DNS trust anchors, TLS floor, remaining headers/privacy, the egress canary, waiver budget & auto-expiry

profiles.name: Gold
profiles.label: Sovereign
profiles.adds: release signing & provenance, Trusted Types everywhere, cross-origin isolation, external signed attestation, ephemeral hermetic build, segregation-of-duties waivers

levels.name: L0
levels.label: Air-Gapped Strict
levels.meaning: Client-side tool with no legitimate network need

levels.name: L1
levels.label: Scoped Egress
levels.meaning: Needs the network, but only to known origins
levels.typical: agent talking to a local LLM or one API

levels.name: L2
levels.label: Public Static
levels.meaning: May include third parties, all non-essential gated
levels.control: no pre-consent egress; trackers behind consent

rules.title: Self-host every runtime dependency
rules.why: The third-party egress set of a surface is the UNION of every host it can reach: all CSP fetch-directive sources (script/style/img/font/media/connect/worker/frame/manifest/prefetch-src) plus every runtime sink (fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, EventSource, WebSocket, new Worker, importScripts, WebAssembly.instantiate*, dynamic import). For L0 that set MUST be a subset of {self}. The canonical breach is a browser OCR/codec engine fetched from a CDN on use — the document stays local, the engine does not.
rules.check:
egress = union(all CSP fetch-dir hosts, all runtime request hosts)
assert egress ⊆ {self}      # not connect-src alone — the whole set
rules.fix: Vendor all assets same-origin; ship the .wasm, workers and data packs from your own origin.

rules.title: Override library default CDN loaders
rules.why: Tesseract.js (workerPath/corePath/langPath → jsDelivr + the tessdata host), jsPDF (the pdfobject viewer → cdnjs), pdf.js workers and ML model loaders all fetch from a CDN by default unless explicitly repointed. The default is invisible egress that CSP-less testing never reveals until it fires.
rules.check:
grep dist: jsdelivr|unpkg|cdnjs|tessdata|projectnaptha => 0 hits
assert every loader path (workerPath/corePath/langPath/…) is same-origin
rules.fix: Pass explicit same-origin paths to every loader; treat a surviving default-CDN literal as a build failure.

rules.title: Same-origin workers; constrain worker-src
rules.why: A Blob worker doing importScripts('https://cdn…'), or a cross-origin module worker, re-introduces code that SRI cannot cover (there is no integrity for importScripts or module workers).
rules.check:
every importScripts(/new Worker( arg resolves same-origin ;
CSP: worker-src 'self' ; child-src 'none'
rules.fix: Bundle workers locally; point any library workerPath at a same-origin file.

rules.title: Constrain connect-src
rules.why: The browser-enforced air-gap for XHR/fetch/WebSocket. connect-src 'none' makes that exfiltration channel impossible regardless of any bug or injection. Tools that genuinely need the network declare an explicit allowlist of exact origins — never '*', never a bare scheme.
rules.check:
parse CSP connect-src:
  L0 => exactly 'none' ; L1 => literal-origin allowlist (no '*'/https:)
  L2 => must exclude every unconsented tracker host
rules.fix: Set connect-src 'none' for pure client-side tools; for an agent talking to a local LLM scope to that exact origin only.

rules.title: No third-party egress during load
rules.why: The air-gap claim must be observable, not asserted. A headless load of the surface must contact NO third-party host: every responding origin is the surface's own. This is the necessary, directly-measurable half of 'works offline' — the network is observed during a normal load, not cut, so it proves no cross-origin dependency fired, not that a full offline smoke test passed.
rules.check:
headless load; assert every responding host is same-origin
(zero third-party responses observed during the load)
rules.fix: Eliminate cross-origin subresources and runtime calls (AG-NET-01/02/04); serve every asset and data pack from your own origin.

rules.title: No third-party connection priming
rules.why: preconnect/dns-prefetch/prefetch to third parties leak intent and warm tracker connections before the visitor interacts at all.
rules.check:
all rel in {preconnect,dns-prefetch,preload,prefetch,modulepreload}
hosts ⊆ {self}
rules.fix: Remove off-origin resource hints; keep only self-targeted preloads.

rules.title: Service Worker hygiene
rules.applies: MUST · when a service worker is registered
rules.why: A service worker is persistent code that intercepts every request and can cache and replay responses. A compromised or over-scoped SW is a durable foothold that survives page reloads.
rules.check:
SW served same-origin ; narrowest scope ; fetch handlers contact
only self ; no remote importScripts ; cache stores only same-origin
rules.fix: Register the narrowest scope; never importScripts a remote URL; restrict the cache to same-origin responses.

rules.title: Violation/error reporting stays same-origin
rules.why: CSP report-to / Reporting-Endpoints / NEL pointed at a third-party SaaS collector silently re-introduces egress and ships metadata about every visitor and violation off-origin — defeating the air-gap through the back door.
rules.check: Reporting-Endpoints / report-to / NEL targets ⊆ {self}  OR  absent
rules.fix: Collect reports at a same-origin endpoint, or disable reporting on air-gapped surfaces.

rules.title: External _blank links sever the opener; privacy surfaces sever the referrer
rules.why: Property: no  exposes window.opener to the destination (reverse tabnabbing). The opener is severed by rel containing 'noopener' OR 'noreferrer' ('noreferrer' implies 'noopener' per the HTML spec). On privacy surfaces the referrer is also suppressed. Browsers now imply noopener for target=_blank by default — treat that as defence-in-depth, not as the control.
rules.check:
for every : rel contains 'noopener' or 'noreferrer' ;
on privacy surfaces rel also contains 'noreferrer'
rules.fix: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to external _blank links; noreferrer also blocks referrer leakage.

rules.title: Ship a CSP
rules.why: A CSP is the single highest-leverage control on a static surface. Header-delivered is preferred; a  CSP is the fallback only for backends that cannot set response headers (GitHub Pages).
rules.check:
response header content-security-policy present
OR  present (record which)
rules.fix: Add the policy at the edge where possible; otherwise emit a meta CSP and accept the AG-CSP-03 limitation.

rules.title: Deny by default; enumerate; forbid bypass primitives
rules.why: A permissive CSP is theatre. The baseline denies by default, enumerates only what is used, and removes every known bypass primitive.
rules.fix: Hash or nonce inline scripts; delete unsafe-eval / unsafe-inline(script) / wildcards; add the missing fetch directives explicitly.

rules.title: Clickjacking control must be header-delivered
rules.why: frame-ancestors, report-uri/report-to and sandbox are IGNORED when a CSP arrives via . A meta-only surface therefore has NO clickjacking protection from frame-ancestors — it must come from an X-Frame-Options header. Where neither header can be set (pure GitHub Pages), the surface MUST be stateless and the residual risk recorded.
rules.check:
if meta-CSP contains frame-ancestors => FAIL (ineffective)
require X-Frame-Options header  OR  declared stateless: true
rules.fix: Move clickjacking control to an XFO header (front with a CDN if the host can't set it), or keep the surface free of auth and state-changing actions.

rules.title: Stage report-only before enforcing
rules.applies: SHOULD · all (mandatory before first enforcing deploy)
rules.why: A CSP that breaks the surface gets disabled in a panic — worse than none. Report-only first turns breakage into telemetry.
rules.check:
Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only canary in staging before the
enforcing policy ships ; violations reviewed
rules.fix: Deploy report-only, watch violations, then promote to enforcing.

rules.title: Force HTTPS subresources
rules.why: A single http:// subresource downgrades the whole page's integrity guarantee.
rules.check: upgrade-insecure-requests present ; grep subresources 'http://' => 0
rules.fix: Add the directive; convert plain-HTTP references to HTTPS or same-origin.

rules.title: Trusted Types for DOM sinks
rules.why: Trusted Types eliminate DOM-XSS by forbidding raw string assignment to injection sinks (innerHTML, script.src, eval). For a tool parsing untrusted input — certificates, uploaded files — this closes the highest-impact client-side bug class outright.
rules.check:
CSP require-trusted-types-for 'script' ;
trusted-types   (no '*'; 'none' if no policy needed)
rules.fix: Enable Trusted Types; route any required HTML through one vetted, sanitizer-backed policy.

rules.title: HSTS with a real max-age
rules.why: max-age=0 DISABLES HSTS and disqualifies the domain from preload while still looking configured — the most common silent regression: the toggle is on, the value is zero.
rules.check:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age >= 31536000; includeSubDomains;
preload      (max-age  FAIL)
rules.fix: Set max-age to one year. On Cloudflare this lives under SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → HSTS — check the value, not just the switch.

rules.title: HSTS scope is sticky — gate it
rules.why: includeSubDomains + preload apply to every subdomain and are hard to reverse. Enable them before a subdomain is permanently on HTTPS and you can lock yourself out of it.
rules.check:
enumerate every subdomain => each returns valid HTTPS
(GitHub Pages: 'Enforce HTTPS' ON) ; record preload submission state
rules.fix: Verify all subdomains over HTTPS first, then add includeSubDomains/preload, then submit to the preload list.

rules.title: Disable MIME sniffing
rules.why: Without nosniff a browser may reinterpret an asset's type and execute content never meant to run.
rules.check: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
rules.fix: Emit the header at the edge / in _headers.

rules.title: X-Frame-Options
rules.why: The reliable, universally-honored clickjacking control; pairs with header CSP frame-ancestors.
rules.check:
X-Frame-Options: DENY  (or SAMEORIGIN only if same-origin
framing is genuinely required)
rules.fix: DENY unless the surface is intentionally self-embedded.

rules.title: Referrer-Policy
rules.why: Stops the surface from leaking the visited URL to outbound links and resources.
rules.check:
Referrer-Policy in { no-referrer,
  strict-origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin }
rules.fix: no-referrer for privacy tools; strict-origin-when-cross-origin for marketing.

rules.title: Permissions-Policy
rules.why: Affirmatively switches off powerful features the surface never uses, including the FLoC/Topics opt-out.
rules.check:
Permissions-Policy disables unused features, e.g.: camera=(),
microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()
rules.fix: Default-deny every feature; open only what the tool needs.

rules.title: Cross-origin isolation for threaded WASM
rules.applies: MUST · when SharedArrayBuffer / threaded WASM is used
rules.why: Threaded/SIMD WASM (e.g. Tesseract with threads) needs SharedArrayBuffer, which requires cross-origin isolation; this also hardens against Spectre-class cross-origin reads.
rules.check:
if SAB used => Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin AND
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
(Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin on served assets)
rules.fix: Set COOP+COEP at the edge; serve assets with CORP same-origin. Not needed for single-threaded WASM.

rules.title: Cache discipline for fingerprinted assets
rules.why: Content-hashed assets are immutable by construction; HTML must never be long-cached or stale tools linger.
rules.check:
hashed assets (/_astro/*, fingerprinted) => Cache-Control: public,
max-age=31536000, immutable ; HTML => no-cache / short
rules.fix: Long-cache hashed bundles, short-cache documents.

rules.title: TLS floor
rules.why: A modern header set over a weak TLS channel is a contradiction. The transport must refuse legacy protocols and ciphers.
rules.check:
min TLS 1.2 (prefer 1.3); no SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1; no RC4/3DES/EXPORT;
OCSP stapling; valid chain
rules.fix: Set the edge/CDN TLS profile to modern; disable legacy protocols/ciphers; enable stapling.

rules.title: CAA pins certificate issuance
rules.why: Without CAA, any public CA can be induced to issue a certificate for your domain. CAA restricts issuance to the CA(s) you actually use and provides an incident contact.
rules.check: dig CAA => issue/issuewild restricted to your ACME CA(s) ; iodef set
rules.fix: Publish CAA on the apex (and wildcards) naming your CA(s); add an iodef mailto.

rules.title: DNSSEC enabled
rules.why: DNSSEC prevents forged DNS answers from silently redirecting your domain.
rules.check: dig +dnssec shows AD ; DS record present at the registrar
rules.fix: Enable DNSSEC at the DNS provider and publish the DS at the registrar.

rules.title: No danglable records (subdomain takeover)
rules.why: A CNAME to a deprovisioned service — a removed Pages site, an unclaimed bucket — is a hijackable subdomain: a live foothold under your brand. Mixed estates (Pages subdomains + a proxied apex) are the usual culprit.
rules.check:
every CNAME target resolves to a claimed/active resource ;
no NXDOMAIN / unclaimed-service takeover fingerprints
rules.fix: Remove or repoint stale records the moment a service is decommissioned.

rules.title: SRI on any unavoidable cross-origin subresource
rules.why: Eliminating cross-origin subresources (AG-NET-01) makes this moot — the strongest answer. Where one must remain, integrity pinning stops a compromised CDN swapping the file.
rules.check:
every cross-origin / has integrity=
AND crossorigin=   ; else FAIL
rules.fix: Prefer self-hosting; otherwise add SRI hashes and re-pin on every version bump.

rules.title: Pin dependencies by integrity hash
rules.why: A floating version is an unsigned cheque to whoever controls the registry or CDN. Pinning by content hash (not just semver) defeats tampering and typosquat republish.
rules.check:
lockfile with integrity hashes committed ; install uses npm ci /
--frozen-lockfile ; no '@latest' / unpinned '@vN' / floating CDN
rules.fix: Commit the lockfile; install frozen; pin any surviving CDN ref to an exact version + SRI.

rules.title: Reproducible build; pinned toolchain
rules.why: A reproducible build is auditable; a drifting toolchain is not.
rules.check:
.nvmrc/engines present ; SSG pinned ; base image pinned by digest ;
build is deterministic
rules.fix: Pin Node, the SSG, and any container base image by digest.

rules.title: No secrets in shipped output
rules.why: The build artifact is public the instant it deploys; a baked token or private key is immediately compromised.
rules.check: secret scan of the BUILD DIR => 0 hits
rules.fix: Scan dist/ in CI; reject on any hit; rotate anything leaked.

rules.title: No unintended source maps
rules.why: Shipped .map files hand an attacker your original source and structure.
rules.check:
no sourceMappingURL / .map served in production
(unless intentional and documented)
rules.fix: Disable production source-map emission, or host maps privately.

rules.title: No known-vulnerable dependencies
rules.why: Shipping a dependency with a known high/critical CVE hands the attacker a public exploit.
rules.check:
vuln scan of resolved deps => 0 high/critical (or each triaged
with a recorded, time-bounded waiver)
rules.fix: Upgrade or replace; gate the build; waive only with justification + expiry.

rules.title: SBOM emitted and retained
rules.why: You cannot respond to the next supply-chain CVE for components you cannot enumerate.
rules.check: CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM produced per build and retained with the release
rules.fix: Generate an SBOM in CI and attach it to the artifact.

rules.title: Signed releases / build provenance
rules.why: Signatures and provenance let consumers verify the artifact is the one your pipeline built, unaltered.
rules.check:
release artifacts signed (Sigstore/cosign or registry provenance);
verification documented
rules.fix: Sign in CI; publish provenance; document verification.

rules.title: Pin third-party Actions/steps to a full commit SHA
rules.why: A mutable tag (@v4) lets the action's owner — or whoever compromises them — change the code you run with repo write access. A 40-hex commit SHA is immutable.
rules.check:
every `uses:` referencing a third party pins a full 40-char
commit SHA (not a tag or branch)
rules.fix: Replace tags with the resolved SHA; let a bot bump SHAs under review.

rules.title: Least-privilege workflow tokens
rules.why: The default workflow token is often write-all; a single compromised step inherits it.
rules.check:
top-level permissions: defaults to read ; write scoped to the
specific job that needs it
rules.fix: Add an explicit minimal permissions: block at workflow and job level.

rules.title: No untrusted code in a privileged context
rules.why: A pull_request_target job (which carries secrets) that checks out and builds/executes the PR head runs attacker-supplied code with your credentials — a classic CI takeover.
rules.check:
no pull_request_target job checks out head.ref AND runs
build/exec/install with access to secrets
rules.fix: Use pull_request (no secrets) for untrusted code, or split so the privileged job never executes PR code.

rules.title: Secrets are not exposed to forks or echoed
rules.why: Secrets reaching fork PRs, or printed to logs, leak to anyone who can open a PR or read a build.
rules.check:
no secret passed to fork-triggered jobs ; no echo/printenv of
${{ secrets.* }} ; masking on
rules.fix: Gate secret-using jobs to trusted events; never print secrets; treat masking as defence-in-depth, not the control.

rules.title: Protected branch with the conformance gate required
rules.why: A standard that isn't a required status check is a suggestion. Make AGSSH a merge gate.
rules.check:
default branch protected ; AGSSH conformance check required ;
no force-push ; review required
rules.fix: Enable branch protection and mark the gate a required status check.

rules.title: Automated contributors run under scoped identity and the same gate
rules.why: Bots and agents that open PRs across many repos are high-value targets and high-blast-radius writers; their commits deserve at least the scrutiny human ones get.
rules.check:
automation uses a scoped token (least repos/permissions), signs
commits, and its PRs pass the AGSSH gate before merge
rules.fix: Scope the automation token; enable commit signing; route automated PRs through the same required gate.

rules.title: Zero telemetry on air-gapped surfaces
rules.why: The correct number of analytics providers on a privacy tool is zero. Anything else contradicts the claim the tool is built on.
rules.check:
zero analytics signatures AND zero third-party requests
(subsumed by AG-NET-01)
rules.fix: Remove analytics entirely; derive usage signal from edge logs you already control if you must.

rules.title: Prior blocking of non-essential third parties
rules.applies: MUST · L0 L1 L2 (decisive at L2)
rules.why: No analytics / ads / embeds / fonts may fire before explicit opt-in. EU law requires PRIOR blocking; exporting IPs to US analytics is a transfer-law exposure. Loading the tracker on page load and letting the visitor decline afterwards is the exact anti-pattern — the cookie is already set and the hit already sent.
rules.check:
first visit, NO consent cookie => zero requests to analytics/ad
hosts AND zero non-essential cookies set
rules.fix: Consent Mode with analytics_storage/ad_storage = denied by default, granted only after explicit consent; wire the banner's accept/decline to actually toggle loading. Or drop third-party analytics for an EU-hosted, cookieless one.

rules.title: Self-host fonts
rules.why: Dynamically embedding Google Fonts has been ruled a privacy violation: it ships the visitor's IP to a third party on every load.
rules.check: zero fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com references
rules.fix: Self-host WOFF2 files in @font-face with font-src 'self'.

rules.title: Minimize storage & fingerprinting
rules.why: Storage and fingerprinting beyond functional need quietly erode the posture and the policy you publish.
rules.check:
enumerate cookies + localStorage on load against an allowlist ;
nothing non-functional present
rules.fix: Keep only what the tool needs; disclose any remaining storage.

rules.title: Cookie attributes where cookies exist
rules.applies: MUST · when any cookie is set
rules.why: A cookie without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite is interceptable, script-readable and CSRF-usable.
rules.check:
every cookie => Secure ; HttpOnly unless a script must read it ;
SameSite=Lax|Strict ; __Host- prefix where applicable
rules.fix: Set the full attribute set; prefer __Host- prefixed cookies.

rules.title: Third-party embeds isolated and consent-gated
rules.why: An embedded video/map/widget sets third-party cookies and runs third-party code; on a privacy surface it is egress and tracking.
rules.check:
L0/L1 => zero third-party iframes ; L2 => embeds sandboxed,
consent-gated, privacy-mode variant or click-to-load facade
rules.fix: Use no-cookie/privacy embeds behind a facade and consent; sandbox the iframe.

rules.title: Neutralize output metadata
rules.why: Generated files leak their toolchain: a PDF's Info dict AND its XMP packet carry Producer/Creator/timestamps (jsPDF embeds these by default); images carry EXIF/GPS/ICC/maker-notes.
rules.check:
sample output => Info + XMP neutralized, creation timestamp
neutral ; image EXIF/GPS/ICC stripped
rules.fix: Set neutral document properties and clear XMP; strip image metadata on processing.

rules.title: Deterministic output
rules.why: Identical inputs yielding byte-identical outputs is both anti-fingerprinting and a reproducibility property.
rules.check: two runs on the same input => identical bytes (modulo intended content)
rules.fix: Zero or fix timestamps and any other non-deterministic fields.

rules.title: In-browser only, no server round-trip
rules.why: The 'nothing is uploaded' claim must hold at the data-flow level: output is produced and delivered locally.
rules.check:
output delivered via Blob/object-URL ; no POST of user content
in the processing path (subsumed by AG-NET-01/04)
rules.fix: Generate and download client-side; remove any upload endpoint from the flow.

rules.title: Waivers can never cover a MUST
rules.why: Conformance integrity needs a hard floor. Every CRITICAL/HIGH MUST is non-waivable by construction; the deviation mechanism exists only for SHOULD items, keeping the load-bearing controls outside any human-justification path.
rules.check:
no entry in deviations[] references a rule whose obligation is MUST
=> any such entry FAILS the gate
rules.fix: Fix the MUST; never waive it. Re-scope to a lower profile only if the rule genuinely does not apply to the surface.

rules.title: Waivers auto-expire; the runner enforces it
rules.why: A waiver without enforced expiry becomes permanent debt. The runner compares expires against now; an expired or missing expiry re-enforces the rule immediately, so a waiver can only ever buy bounded time — a fake far-future date still decays on renewal.
rules.check: every deviation has expires  the rule is re-enforced (fail)
rules.fix: Set a real, short expiry; renew under review or remediate.

rules.title: Deviation budget / debt ceiling
rules.why: Truthfulness cannot be machine-judged, but volume can be capped. A per-surface ceiling on the count and weight of active deviations makes waiving-to-green structurally impossible past the budget.
rules.check: sum(active deviation weights)  else FAIL
rules.fix: Pay down debt before adding more; the budget forces remediation over accumulation.

rules.title: Segregation of duties on waivers
rules.why: A self-approved waiver is no control. Each deviation must be signed by an authorized approver distinct from the change author — turning a waiver into an attributable, accountable act rather than anonymous YAML.
rules.check:
each deviation carries approver != author AND a signature
verifiable against an approver allowlist
rules.fix: Route waivers through a named approver; sign them; reject self-approval.

rules.title: Conformance record is externally derived and signed
rules.why: A record produced inside a compromised build host can be forged. The authoritative record is produced by an independent runner observing the LIVE deployed surface — headers, egress, DNS and TLS are externally observable — and is signed and bound to the artifact digest, so build-host compromise cannot fabricate production reality.
rules.check:
record generated against the live URL by an out-of-band runner ;
signed (in-toto / cosign) ; bound to artifact digest ; signature verifies
rules.fix: Run the gate against production from a separate trusted runner; sign the attestation; verify on consumption.

rules.title: Active egress canary - prove the wall, do not observe its silence
rules.why: Observing 'no egress during a test' proves a negative and is defeated by env-detecting, time-delayed or interaction-gated exfiltration. Instead the harness injects a known exfil probe and asserts the policy BLOCKS it — a positive test of a capability boundary that holds in production for every visitor regardless of attacker timing. CSP is the boundary; the canary proves it is real.
rules.check:
synthetic beacon to a non-allowlisted origin (fetch/img/beacon/ws)
is blocked by CSP ; a violation is recorded ; production same-origin
reporting is collecting
rules.fix: Lock every fetch-directive to self (AG-NET-01); add the blocked-probe test; collect violation reports same-origin in production.
rules.tool: chromedp + injected probe + CSP report endpoint

rules.title: Build environment is ephemeral and hermetic
rules.why: A persistent build agent is a persistent foothold that can tamper outputs after the gate. A fresh isolated runner per build, a base image pinned by digest, and short-lived OIDC credentials shrink the window in which the host can forge results — and pair with external verification (AG-GOV-05) so tampering is contradicted by the production scan.
rules.check:
build runs on a fresh ephemeral runner ; base image pinned by
digest ; credentials are short-lived OIDC (no long-lived secrets on agent)
rules.fix: Use ephemeral CI runners, digest-pinned images and OIDC federation instead of stored secrets.
